utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: I can help with the repair drive—what needs fixing first?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thanks, Leo. The roof over the shed is leaking badly, so that ought to come first if you don’t mind.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Makes sense. I’ll bring a ladder and tarp—can you have the ladder area cleared before I get there?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Kira, I’m willing to help, but we should pin down who’s bringing tools and where everything’s being dropped off first.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Can we confirm the tool list and the drop-off spot before anyone starts hauling things over?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Yes, let’s do that first—if we don’t sort the tool list and a single drop-off spot, people will show up with the wrong things and it’ll turn messy fast.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh—right, the repair drive. Are we still meeting by the community shed, or did that change?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: I think it’s still the community shed—unless I mixed it up with the tool swap again. Maybe we should head there first and check.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Yeah, let’s do that—I probably missed an update somewhere, so the shed’s the safest bet.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I heard there’s a repair drive coming up, and I’m telling folks so more neighbors can join in.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s good to hear—I can mention it while I’m out and about. Just tell me when and where it’s happening.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Ira—I’m still waiting on the exact time and place, but as soon as I hear, I’ll pass it along so you can spread the word too.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry I’m late—how’s the repair drive shaping up, Gus?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: No worries, Dane—we’ve got a decent start, and a few folks already dropped off busted lamps and toasters. If you’ve got a minute, I could use an extra pair of hands sorting tools.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Yeah, absolutely—I can jump in and sort tools wherever you need me.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s keep the repair drive simple and organized so folks know exactly what to bring and when.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely—if we lock the details tonight, I can start inviting everyone right away and make sure they know exactly what to bring and when to show up.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Good—let’s set it for Saturday from 10 to noon at the community shed, and ask folks to bring small appliances, lamps, and tools they can carry themselves.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Sam, how many people have actually signed up for the repair drive so far?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I haven’t seen the latest count yet, but I can check with the organizers and let you know.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Please do, and ask whether they still need more volunteers or specific tools.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Opal, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—want me to help connect a few folks who’d be into it?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Yes, please—if you can, connect me with anyone on Maple, Cedar, and the south end of Birch, since I’m tracking who’s close enough to drop items off easily.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely—I can reach out to a few people on Maple and Cedar, and I know someone on the south end of Birch who’d likely be interested too.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Absolutely, Rosa — I’m still on board for the repair drive and can help with setup if you need me.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s wonderful, Mara, thank you. Could you come by a little early on Saturday to help set up the tables and signage?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Of course, Rosa — I can come by early Saturday and help with the tables and signage. Just tell me what time you’d like me there.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ve got a decent count on tape, gloves, and bottled water for the repair drive, but we’re a bit short on work lights. Do you want me to ask around the block for a few more?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Yeah, ask around for a few work lights. I’m juggling three things, so keep it simple and just text me the count.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Will do — I’ll ask around the block and text you how many work lights I can line up.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hey Rey, I heard the repair drive’s shaping up nicely—sounds like folks are bringing tools and spare parts already.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Yeah, that’s good to hear. I was thinking I could stop by with a screwdriver set and see what else people still need.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be perfect—word is they could really use basic hand tools, and I heard Mara might bring extension cords too. If you go, let me know what’s still missing and I’ll pass it around.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before we set anything up, can you remind me which repairs the drive is covering and who’s organizing pickups?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: It’s for small household fixes and bike repairs, and I’m pretty sure Malik is coordinating the pickups. I can double-check the list after school drop-off if you want.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, that helps — could you double-check both the repair list and whether Malik’s definitely handling pickups after drop-off?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: I’m in for the repair drive—just tell me when and what to bring.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s great, Bo—thank you. I’ll let you know the time soon, and for now just plan on bringing any basic tools you’ve got handy.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Perfect—send me the time when you’ve got it, and I’ll bring my basic tools.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Jules, I’m spreading the word that we’re doing the repair drive soon, so folks know to bring their broken stuff by.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Love that—I'll mention it to the garden crew and the parents' chat so a few more people hear about it.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Perfect, I’ll keep telling people too so the repair drive really gets around.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh—right, the repair drive. I meant to swing by and help, did you say it was this Saturday?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Yeah, this Saturday. If you can make it, that’d help a lot.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Yeah, I think I can make it—what time should I come by again?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I heard a little about it, but not much yet. What kind of repairs are folks bringing in?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Mostly small stuff—wobbly chairs, lamps that quit, bike tune-ups, that sort of thing. I told folks I can bring my tools and help with anything simple we can fix on a table.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds nice and manageable. Do you know if anyone’s bringing sewing or mending too, or is it mostly tools-and-parts kind of fixes?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Opal—I'm glad we’re getting the repair drive moving. I’ve got a simple signup sheet ready, so we can match neighbors with the jobs they need help with.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: That’s a solid start, Rosa. If you want, I can add addresses or building numbers to the signup so we know exactly where each repair request is.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That would be perfect, Opal—thank you. Add the addresses and building numbers, and I’ll sort the list by block so we can keep the day running smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m fine helping, but have we sorted where people should drop items off and who’s hauling the bulky stuff?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Not fully yet, so I’m going to ask around today and get a drop-off spot plus a couple of folks with trucks lined up fast.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Okay, that helps—I just don’t want donations piling up with nowhere to go, so let me know the drop-off spot before we tell too many people.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Are we sure the repair drive is actually happening this weekend? I just want to confirm before I commit anything.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I haven’t confirmed it myself yet, so I don’t want to assume. Let me check who finalized the schedule before you commit.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Okay, thanks—can you let me know once someone’s actually confirmed the schedule? I’d rather not plan around it until we know for sure.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s keep it simple, Dane: make a short list of the repairs, then we can decide what to tackle first.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry, I’m late again — I’d start with the fence, the porch steps, and that leaky gutter, then we can pick the worst one first.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That works for me, Dane. Let’s look at the fence, porch steps, and gutter in that order, and pick whichever needs doing most urgently.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I only heard bits and pieces—do you know if they’ve started collecting supplies yet for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Yeah, they started this week—I’ve seen folks dropping off tools and spare parts at the community hall already.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh good, that’s farther along than I thought. I only heard second-hand that they were getting organized, so maybe I should swing by the hall and see what they still need.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh right, the repair drive—sorry, it slipped my mind for a second. I meant to ask if we’re still meeting by the community shed.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Yep, still by the community shed—same time as planned. I’ll bring the signup sheet and a box for small tool donations.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Got it, community shed at the usual time—thanks for reminding me. I’ll try to bring that spare screwdriver set, assuming I don’t leave it on my kitchen table again.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help with the repair drive, but I need to work around school pickup and drop-off times.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: That works—just come by when you’re free between pickups, and I’ll keep a couple of easy jobs aside for you.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Perfect, I can swing by mid-morning after drop-off and stay until I need to head back for pickup.
